title: Global Higher Education & Internationalization
subtitle: a graduate-level guide to internationalization strategy, from Knight's definition to decolonizing the partnership, with a strategy explorer, a rankings explorer, a TNE selector and a self-check
problem: Senior international officers, provosts and the graduate students who will replace them inherit an internationalization strategy that is really a list: a study-abroad office, a few memoranda, a recruitment agent contract, a ranking to chase. Each lever is treated as the strategy; the rationales, the systems on the other side of the partnership and the power asymmetries in the flows are rarely examined together.
solution: A seventeen-section resource that starts from Knight's definition and the four rationales, sets out the levers of comprehensive internationalization in a strategy explorer, follows student mobility and services across the lifecycle, reads comparative systems and the Bologna Process in depth, opens up what three global rankings actually reward, weighs transnational-education models in a selector, presents virtual exchange as an equity strategy, walks the partnership lifecycle and funding programmes, and confronts decolonization and equity — closing with a comprehensive-internationalization self-check after Hudzik.
pedagogy: strategy as a set of choices with trade-offs: every explorer pairs a lever, ranking or TNE model with its benefits and the challenges leaders must manage; general patterns are labelled as patterns, never as statistics; the self-check makes the reader assess their own institution before the page suggests what comprehensive looks like.
